claim: Defines the object token O_{tau,n} representing the state of player or ball n at time tau: a learned identity I_n, 3D position p, 3D velocity v, distance-to-ball d, and elapsed time e.
equation: O_{\tau,n} = \{I_n, (p_{x,\tau,n}, p_{y,\tau,n}, p_{z,\tau,n}), (v_{x,\tau,n}, v_{y,\tau,n}, v_{z,\tau,n}), (d_{x,\tau,n}, d_{y,\tau,n}, d_{z,\tau,n}), e \}

claim: Defines the model's predictive distribution: the probability that object n moves to bin location k at the next step tau+1, given the history of its object tokens, computed by model f.
Samples the next-step bin location rho from the predictive distribution; the updated position, velocity, and distance-to-ball are then computed from the bin-to-physical-distance mapping.
Rolls out simulations autoregressively: at step i the bin location is sampled from the distribution conditioned on up to T previous token steps, with missing tokens padded with zeros and masked.
equation: \rho_{i} \sim p(\rho_{i} = k | O_{i-1}, O_{i-2} \ldots O_{i - T})

claim: States the 2D-only assumption for players: the vertical (z) components of player position and velocity are zero; for the ball, distance-to-ball d is set to 0.
Defines the generic-player initialization: the generic model f_gen learns a single shared identity vector I_gen for all players before per-player fine-tuning transfers a new I_n.
